result.instructions: Use assess_trip for ordinary synthetic driver or dispatcher trip questions. Extract only facts supported by the user's words. requester_role is who is asking; subject_role is the assessed person (truck_driver or other). Do not infer subject identity from requester. Use trip_dispatch for 'can I take/send this truck', terminal_entry for gate-only questions, and induction only when explicitly asked. Missing intent stays unknown. Record quantities with explicit units; ask about ambiguous units. Do not invent IDs or dates. For relative dates, obtain an explicit date/time/timezone before filling trip_at. Leave unavailable facts absent or null. Save the returned trip_id and revision in the conversation. Follow-up answers and explicit corrections use update_trip_facts. Use case.revision for updates. write_receipt records the original write and can be older after a retry; the assessment uses the latest saved case. If an update conflicts with another writer, reassess by trip_id before retrying; don't guess a revision. Lead with the scoped finding and the most relevant next questions; keep technical IDs out of ordinary user-facing answers. Distinguish reported facts, synthetic evidence, archived sources, and unexecuted requirements. If service_status is unavailable, say the facts were saved but assessment is unavailable. Never convert pressure, a permit report, or induction success into entry/dispatch clearance. This connector accepts synthetic development cases only, not real driver identifiers or credentials.

tools.description: Legacy single-call synthetic APM induction check, retained for regression replay. For ordinary driver or dispatcher trip conversations, use assess_trip and update_trip_facts so the same assignment and corrections are retained. This tool queries server-owned synthetic completion evidence from the user's supplied facts. Missing facts stay null and callers cannot supply evidence. Returns one induction finding and unchecked trip coverage, never real verification or dispatch clearance.

company_changed.description: Whether the user reports a company change. This does not establish a SeaLink change.

current_sealink_id.description: Current synthetic SeaLink alias; never substitute an old identifier or invent one.

driver_id.description: Synthetic driver alias supplied by the user, not a real driver identifier. Do not guess.

terminal_id.description: APM Elizabeth ID, the synthetic other terminal, or null if unknown.

trip_at.description: Exact supplied trip timestamp including seconds and timezone. Use null if absent; never use today's date to fill it.

observations.source_locator: Archived NJPASS home HTML, Bulletin panel
observations.source_text: Effective August 3, 2026, a section of Port St. will be reduced to one lane in both directions between Brewster Rd. and Marlin St. until further notice. In this section of Port St., lanes will be reduced to 11 feet wide and all oversize loads heading eastbound on Port St. MUST utilize the Corbin St. ramp. All oversize loads heading westbound on Port St. MUST follow the Marlin St. / Kellogg St. detour or utilize Outer Port St. until further notice. All oversize loads MUST exit through the south via North Ave. Please call the Port Authority Police Department (PAPD) at (973) 578-2180 to request an escort for any oversize loads travelling through the port.
